name: Counsel memo on a tightly specified messenger flow
decision_question: May a paid company convey a consumer's undisputed cancellation decision (messenger only), and can providers refuse it?
method: Brief Japanese counsel (consumer-contract and Attorney Act experience) with the flow in report §N.3 and legal-matrix questions L01-L05, L11, L18, L21, L22
measures: Counsel's view on each question, with confidence and conditions
proceed_rule: Written view that (a) undisputed conveyance as messenger is unlikely to be a 'legal matter' AND (b) there is a reliable basis for provider acceptance (current law or the planned reform) AND (c) route-level outcome data can be reused in some processed form
kill_rule: Any of (a)-(c) answered negatively, or answered 'depends on each provider's terms' with no reform route, so the concierge variant (C04/C05) STOPS
decision_value: Very high: binary gate on stop conditions 2 and 9
value_per_effort_rationale: One document decides whether any hard-route product can exist. Cheapest decisive step.

name: Activity-selected reconstruction of real cancellations
decision_question: Does a definable segment hit hard-route cancellations (phone, written, in person) often enough, and would they have handed them over?
method: Japanese 45-minute interviews. Participants open their own statements and app subscription lists on screen (no sharing of credentials or files); reconstruct the last 3 cancellations or attempts and all current recurring charges by rail
sample: 15-20 adults who cancelled or tried to cancel ≥1 subscription in the past 12 months; quota for 50+ and for parents of school-age children
measures: Rail of each charge; route class of each attempted cancellation; steps and minutes as remembered; outcome (stopped, persisted, gave up); whether anyone else did it; what was paid
proceed_rule: ≥30% of participants had ≥1 hard-route cancellation in 12 months AND ≥half of those had someone else do it or gave up and kept paying
kill_rule: <10% had a hard-route cancellation, or most hard-route cases were solved in one call
depends_on: None (can run in parallel with E5)
decision_value: High: the only way to measure B1 rail mix and J4 frequency
value_per_effort_rationale: Public data cannot answer B1 or frequency. Cheap relative to its effect on stop conditions 1, 4 and 6.

name: Partner willingness-to-pay probe (B2B2C)
decision_question: Will a Japanese issuer, bank, wallet or benefits provider pay at least the C07 floor for cancellation-and-verification?
method: Structured conversations with product owners (prior behaviour: have they bought or built recurring-payment controls? What do disputes cost them?)
sample: 3-5 organisations: one megabank not owning a PFM, one card issuer, one wallet, one benefits provider
measures: Existing tooling; dispute and chargeback cost; stated budget band; competing options (network tooling, own PFM)
proceed_rule: ≥1 organisation states a budget at or above ¥18 per enrolled user-month (tight-illustration floor at 50k enrolled) and pilot interest
kill_rule: All prefer network tooling or their own PFM, or no budget
depends_on: E5 (needed to describe a lawful service)
value_per_effort_rationale: Decides the only model whose margins improve with low frequency.

name: Extended route-coverage and terms review (desk)
decision_question: Across a defined provider set, how many routes are B vs hard, and do any provider terms accept company agents?
method: Extend 04_CANCELLATION_ROUTE_MATRIX.csv to 40 providers chosen by category weight (including cosmetics and supplement 定期購入 sellers and gyms not yet sampled); open each provider's terms and help pages when page access is available
measures: Route class; explicit agent, proxy, family-only or holder-only language; channel; deadlines; fees
proceed_rule: ≥1 major provider in an E-class category documents acceptance of a non-family agent
kill_rule: 0 of 40 accept company agents and ≥10 restrict to the holder or family (stop condition 2 strengthened)
authorisation_needed: None (public research), but page access is needed (egress currently blocked)
value_per_effort_rationale: Closes the sampling bias (the current sample leans to easy, large providers) at no cash cost.

name: Manual concierge on hard routes (founder-run, not presented as automated)
decision_question: What are request-to-verified-stop minutes, interventions and failure reasons on hard routes, and do they fall with volume?
method: With signed per-case instructions from consenting users; the founder conveys the cancellation; the user performs any authentication; verify on the next statement shared on screen
measures: Minutes per case (split handoff, call, rework); contacts; user interventions; acceptance; effective date; next-cycle charge state; failure reason; learning curve over cases
proceed_rule: Median ≤30 minutes AND ≥80% verified stop AND minutes falling across cases
kill_rule: Median above the C04 frontier at the tested fee, OR <60% verified stop, OR providers refuse the messenger in most cases
authorisation_needed: Live user accounts, cancellations, outreach (all currently unauthorised)
value_per_effort_rationale: Measures the minute frontier and M1 learning directly. Expensive and legally gated, so ranked after E5 and PR1.

name: Verification by rail
decision_question: Can a later charge (or its absence) reliably confirm cancellation on each rail?
method: Piggyback on E3: classify each case's rail and whether the next statement or list proves the stop
measures: Share verifiable by rail; days to verification; false 'stopped' (e.g. term contracts)
proceed_rule: ≥80% verifiable on card or bank rails
kill_rule: Card or bank verification <60% because of descriptor mismatch
value_per_effort_rationale: Cheap add-on; defines where 'verified stop' is real.

name: Expert interviews (provider support lead; open-banking operator; consumer-law specialist; contact-centre operator)
decision_question: Do provider support teams accept messengers in practice? What do minutes and identity checks really cost?
method: 4 interviews about prior practice, not opinions on the product
measures: Acceptance policy in practice; identity-check steps; handling time norms; partner pricing norms
proceed_rule: A support lead confirms that messenger calls with a written instruction are accepted in their operation
value_per_effort_rationale: Informal confirmation of E1 and E5 at low cost.

name: Merchant-descriptor normalisation on consented, redacted data
decision_question: How accurately can recurring charges be mapped to providers and rails?
method: Participant-redacted statement extracts; manual labelling; compare simple rules vs incumbents' known limits
measures: Precision and recall by rail; share of aggregate descriptors
authorisation_needed: Use of participants' financial data (consented); not the founder's own
value_per_effort_rationale: Incumbents already detect on card rails (M2 is a feature). Run only for a partner build.
